abstract: Transcriptomic and proteomic studies have characterized host responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection, yet changes in endogenous enzymatic activities remain poorly understood. Here, we screened 89 enzyme-activatable fluorescence probes in living SARS-CoV-2-infected Calu-3 cells and identified 18 probes showing enhanced fluorescence, with some exhibiting multiplicity-of-infection-dependent responses. Neither SARS-CoV-2 Mpro nor PLpro activated the tested probes, and several did not exhibit comparable fluorescence enhancements in influenza-virus-infected cells. Target identification and biochemical validation implicated calpain-1 (CAPN1) and puromycin-sensitive aminopeptidase (PSA) as major contributors to probe activation. A PSA-reactive fluorescence probe confirmed that SARS-CoV-2-infected living cells showed enhanced PSA activity, which was suppressed by puromycin. Immunofluorescence analysis revealed a strong positive correlation between PSA and SARS-CoV-2 spike protein signals. Notably, neither CAPN1 nor PSA was included among differentially expressed genes or proteins previously identified in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells. These findings highlight activity-based fluorescence screening as a complementary strategy to expression-based analyses for discovering infection-induced biomarker enzymes.
